name: Ethiopia Organic Limu G2
vendor_notes: Fruity with lime citrus, herbal and floral notes. Chocolaty and complex. Brightness 6/7, body 4/7, sweetness 3/7, complexity 7/7.
goal: Bright, fruity, floral light roast for espresso
rationale: High-grown (1,900 m) washed heirloom beans are small and dense: they take heat well and need a strong start, or the roast runs out of momentum and tastes flat. The lime and floral notes are fragile, so development stays short (DTR ~18%, ~9-10 C after FC). Sweetness is the weak spot (3/7), and light Ethiopians can be sour as espresso, so development isn't cut to the bone. If shots are sour or thin, add 10-15 s of development first.
steps: Preheat to 195 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 195. Burner 75%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 110 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 179 C (~6:11): burner 47%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:20 at ~189 C: burner 42%, air 50. Then 37%.
Drop ~8:55 at ~198.5 C (9.5 C after FC).

rest.note: Dense, light-roasted washed Ethiopian degasses slowly. Before about day 10 shots run fast, foamy and sour; the lime and florals settle in around two weeks.

history.note: Initial plan from vendor data (Coffee Bean Corral) and Kaleido M1 behaviour. FC temperature is a guess until your first roast calibrates the probe.

No usable roast yet (roast 1 discarded). v2 applies what the decaf and Honduras roasts showed: TP ~0:40 on this drum, steady 10+ min preheat, lower charge burner, burner steps ~2 min before FC. FC 189 C is an estimate from the Honduras (188.9 C).

Re-fitted the first 3-4 minutes to five real roasts (2026-09-29 to 10-02): on this roaster TP comes at ~0:35 at 108-116 C (not ~0:42 at ~100 C), RoR is highest right after TP and only falls, dry end lands ~3:35-3:55 and FC ~7:12-7:25 at 187-189 C. Earlier versions put the start 10-20 C too low, which invited cutting heat early and a hot finish. FC temperature, roast level and development are unchanged.
